source.title: The Effect of Label Noise on the Information Content of Neural Representations
source.authors: Ali Hussaini Umar; Franky Kevin Nando Tezoh; Jean Barbier; Santiago Acevedo; Alessandro Laio

record.file_problem: The supplied text contains the paper and appendix. It has apparent typographical and equation-formatting errors, but the relevant results are readable.
record.tranche_reason: The study sweeps network width and reports test-error curves with double descent, using its own FCNN and CNN settings rather than the version's specified one-hidden-layer ReLU settings.
record.gate_note: The study reports test-error behavior across width and label-noise conditions. Other reported information-imbalance measurements concern representation similarity or performance and do not measure the magnitude-aware sharpness in V7.
record.test_reason: The study directly varies network width and measures held-out classification error, the method and measure relevant to V2. Its MNIST FCNN and CIFAR-10 CNN curves exhibit a second descent at large widths. The CNN experiment extends the architectural setting.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate but incomplete. The authors also conclude that strongly overparameterized hidden representations are approximately robust to moderate label noise, while information loss near the output increases with noise. Random-label representations can underperform random features. They propose information imbalance as an unsupervised indicator of representation quality; their performance evidence is correlational.
record.recipe_differences: Width sweeps with mini-batch SGD and cross-entropy on MNIST and CIFAR-10; label noise is varied and representation information imbalance is measured. The paper does not state whether explicit regularization is used.
record.method_sensitivity: Test error and representation information vary with width, dataset, and label-noise level; the underparameterized label-noise effect differs between MNIST and CIFAR-10.

fits_no_version.finding: Underparameterized label corruption reduces MNIST test error but does not significantly change CIFAR-10 test error.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Label corruption can improve held-out performance in some underparameterized classification settings.

fits_no_version.finding: Information imbalance between independently initialized hidden representations resembles double descent and approaches zero at large widths.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Hidden representations become less mutually predictive near the test-error peak and more mutually predictive at larger widths.

fits_no_version.finding: Noisy-label representations are marginally more informative at small widths; clean-label representations become more informative in the modern regime, with approximate equivalence at very large widths.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The relative information content of clean-label and noisy-label representations depends on network width.

fits_no_version.finding: Lower hidden-to-pre-softmax information imbalance accompanies lower cross-entropy loss.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Hidden-to-output information imbalance correlates with classification performance in these models.

fits_no_version.finding: Random-label representations can be less informative than random features, and clean-task classifiers using them perform worse.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Random-label representation learning can impair downstream clean-task performance relative to random features.

record.problems: The study uses baseline FCNN and CNN architectures on MNIST and CIFAR-10; the authors say extension to more realistic datasets and architectures would be useful. Key width-sweep values are figure-only in the supplied text, with no reported uncertainty estimates. The study does not state whether explicit regularization is used.
record.rows_left_out: No reported claim-relevant results omitted; reported figure-only width-sweep outcomes are represented as figure-only rows because the supplied text provides no numeric values.

untested.parts: No paired measurements establish near-perfect random-label fitting, natural-label generalization, and chance held-out performance after direct random-label training.

The supplied text does not establish training to convergence, absence of explicit regularization, activation functions, or measured widths attaining zero training error. It does not test a one-hidden-layer network on downsampled CIFAR-10.
FCNN and CNN are evaluated on different datasets; there is no controlled architectural comparison or local-connectivity intervention.
No batch-size comparison; batch size is fixed at 128.
No magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness, generalization-gap ranking, or comparison with norm- and margin-based measures.
No removal of memorized examples and retraining comparison.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source for V2. Verdicts use explicit descriptions in the supplied text because plot values are unavailable. Missing recipe details are untested conditions, not evidence of failure. States for rows linked to none indicate that those measures cannot determine a listed version, rather than rejecting the reported findings.

versions.untested_parts: The study trains with random labels in one experiment, but does not report whether the same network and recipe fit those labels almost perfectly, nor held-out accuracy for a network trained directly on random labels.

The study tests width-dependent test error on its single-layer FCNN/MNIST and four-stage CNN/CIFAR-10 setups. It does not test the specified one-hidden-layer ReLU networks on downsampled CIFAR-10, nor explicitly state that these runs use no explicit regularization or train to convergence.
It uses both FCNN and CNN architectures but does not compare their test errors on the same image task and training setup.
It measures information imbalance and its relation to cross-entropy loss, but not magnitude-aware sharpness or the version's comparison with norm- and margin-based measures.
